Observations: Channel 0, 1, and 4 have large W1 L2 norms across the playable 8Ã8 area but are near zero on the same internal wall cells, e.g. channel 0 has low values at (4,4)=0.29, (4,5)=0.37, (5,4)=0.42, (5,5)=0.36, while high values appear on free cells such as (4,2)=16.48 and (5,7)=13.86. Channel 1 shows the same wall/free pattern. Channel 2 is sparse and sharply peaked only at two cells: (2,4)=4.90 and (6,4)=4.50. Channel 3 is nearly uniform over the whole grid, with values around 0.3â0.49, suggesting a constant/bias-like channel. Channel 4 is again high on free cells and low on the internal walls. The output biases are b3 = [-0.873, 0.703, 0.712, 0.595, -0.092], so no-op is suppressed and movement actions are generally preferred. A strong target-related weight appears in unit 6: (r2,c4,ch2) = -4.876, matching one of the two sparse channel-2 cells.

Reasoning: The fixed wall patternâcentral 2Ã2 block and symmetric side wallsâplus exactly two fixed special cells at (2,4) and (6,4) is characteristic of a Sokoban level. The channels that are high across all free cells but low on walls are consistent with floor, box, and agent one-hot encodings, while the sparse channel 2 marks fixed targets. The action set is only no-op plus four movement directions; in Sokoban, pushing is automatic when the agent moves into a box, so no separate push/pickup action is needed. This rules out games requiring pickup/drop/toggle actions, and the two fixed targets rule out simple maze/goal games with a single random goal. The wall layout and target placement strongly match a small Sokoban puzzle.

Game: Sokoban.

Description: The agent moves around a grid maze and pushes boxes onto target squares. Reward is given for placing boxes on the targets, typically all boxes must be on targets to solve the level.

Confidence: 92%
